title: Comparison 1 · Quantify rotation-interpolation differences
summary: Run two Rotates differing only in interpolation (nearest vs linear), subtract the results, and read the min / max / sigma from stats.moments to put numbers on the mismatch.

steps.title: Quantify an image difference
steps.body:
Running two Rotates that differ only in interpolation and eyeballing the previews is intuitive — but you can't say *how much* they differ.

In this tutorial:

  1. **arith.binop (op=sub)** builds a difference image → one glance shows where the two disagree.
  2. **stats.moments** reports min / max / mean / sigma on the diff → you can state the discrepancy numerically.

The diff + stats pattern is the single most common 'behavioural difference' visualisation in image processing — worth adding to your toolkit.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Checkerboard**. Sharp edges maximise interpolation differences, making it the ideal input for this comparison.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.checker` shows its image before we start wiring filters.

steps.title: Drop Rotate #1 (for nearest)
steps.body: From Geometry, drag **Rotate** — this one will be the nearest side.

steps.title: Wire Checker → Rotate #1
steps.body: Drag from Checkerboard's `image` output to Rotate #1's `image` input.

steps.title: Click Rotate #1
steps.body: Click Rotate #1. We'll set `angle_deg` and `interpolation`.

steps.title: Set angle_deg to 15
steps.body: Enter **15** in `angle_deg`. An off-grid angle forces interpolation on every pixel.

steps.title: Set interpolation to nearest
steps.body: Change `interpolation` to `nearest`.

steps.title: Drop Rotate #2 (for linear)
steps.body: Drag another **Rotate**. Place it next to Rotate #1.

steps.title: Wire Checker → Rotate #2
steps.body: Drag from the *same* Checkerboard `image` output to the new Rotate #2's `image` input.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. `geom.rotate`'s default behaviour becomes a baseline before we tune angle and interpolation.

steps.title: Click Rotate #2
steps.body: Click Rotate #2.

steps.title: Set angle_deg to 15 (same)
steps.body: Enter **15** — same angle as Rotate #1 so the only difference is the interpolation method.

steps.title: Set interpolation to linear
steps.body: Change `interpolation` to `linear`.

steps.title: Drop the Arithmetic node
steps.body: From Arithmetic, drag **Arithmetic · a ∘ b** (`arith.binop`). It has two inputs (`a`, `b`) and emits the result of the op chosen by the `op` dropdown (add / sub / mul / div).

steps.title: Wire Rotate #1 (nearest) → arith.binop.a
steps.body: Drag from Rotate #1's `image` output to `arith.binop.a`.

steps.title: Wire Rotate #2 (linear) → arith.binop.b
steps.body: Drag from Rotate #2's `image` output to `arith.binop.b`.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. With default `op=add` the result is nearest + linear — a baseline before we flip the op to sub.

steps.title: Click arith.binop
steps.body: Click arith.binop. Default `op` is `add` — we want the difference, so switch to `sub`.

steps.title: Set op to sub
steps.body: Change `op` to **`sub`**. Output becomes `a − b = nearest − linear`.

steps.title: Drop the Statistics node
steps.body: From Statistics, drag **Statistics (FS)**. It summarises the diff image into numbers.

steps.title: Wire arith.binop.out → Statistics.image
steps.body: Drag from arith.binop's `out` output to Statistics' `image` input.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body:
Press ▶ Run graph. Four nodes execute (Rotate ×2 → arith.binop → Statistics). What to look at:

  • **arith.binop's preview image** — bright/dark bands sit along the checker edges. That's where nearest and linear disagree. Flat regions (pure white / black) have diff ≈ 0 → uniform grey.
  • **Statistics' numbers** — `min` / `max` give the amplitude of the diff; `sigma` gives the typical mismatch size. Identical interpolation → everything 0; a 15° rotation should produce non-zero values.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body:
The diff-image + stats pattern is a daily tool in real cryo-EM for asking "how much did my change affect the result?".

**Play with it:**
  • Set `angle_deg` to 0 / 45 / 90 — integer-friendly angles shrink the diff (nearest ≈ linear), half-pixel angles maximise it.
  • Swap input to Siemens Star / Noise — edge-rich images blow up the sigma (= interpolation effects live at high frequency).
  • Switch one Rotate's `interpolation` to `cubic` / `quintic` to compare cubic vs linear.
  • Flip arith.binop's `op` to `div` for a ratio image, `mul` for masked diff — four ops from the same node.
